subject: Next steps & model parity: PayGrid model-fit eval

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@paygrid.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: PayGrid discovery — model-fit eval follow-up

Hi Elena / Samir — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our side: 

1) Summary from the call:
- Primary goal: reduce false positives in merchant risk scoring while keeping latency <= 200ms median for inference at 512 tokens.
- Current baseline: PayGrid uses a proprietary in-house transformer (~2B params) for reranking.
- Success metric: parity with proprietary baseline on PayGrid QA set (acceptance threshold: within 2% F1) and no more than 10% latency regression.

2) Redwood suggested approach:
- Run a model-fit eval comparing a shortlist of open models (Llama-3-13B-Chat, Vicuna-13B-1.5, Mistral-Instruct-7B) plus Redwood-optimized quantized variants vs your baseline.
- We'll use the prompt set we discussed and your labeled QA slices (anonymized).
- Deliverables: benchmark spreadsheet with accuracy/latency/cost, prompt set, and an executive summary with recommendations.

3) Ask from PayGrid:
- Can you share the current sample QA set (anonymized) and an approximate QPS / peak concurrency profile?

4) Next steps / timeline:
- I attached the prompt set we typically start with (paygrid_eval_prompt_set.csv) and our example benchmark report (open_model_benchmarks.md).
- If you can send the sample QA by EOD Friday (6/12), we can run a first-pass eval by 6/16 and share a parity summary.

Attach: paygrid_eval_prompt_set.csv, open_model_benchmarks.md

Thanks — looping in our SEs for technical alignment: Aditya Rao (solutions), Rishi Malhotra (inference).

Best,

Hi Elena / team — jumping in with the technical plan and initial recommendations. Short answers up front: 

- Recommended shortlist for model-fit eval (balanced accuracy, latency, and cost):
  * Mistral-Instruct-7B (FP16 / 4-bit quantized) — strong instruction-following with good compute efficiency
  * Llama-3-13B-Chat (float16, tuned) — better contextual understanding often helpful for nuanced risk cases
  * Falcon-40B-Instruct (quantized variant) — will be a heavier baseline if you're willing to accept higher infra cost for quality gains

- Why these: we prioritized models that have demonstrated parity potential on classification/reranking tasks while remaining cost-effective when quantized and served with Redwood kernels.

- Evaluation plan:
  1) Run closed eval on the anonymized QA set you provide against your baseline and each candidate model using the supplied prompt set.
  2) Measure: macro F1, precision@k, latency median/P95 at your qps profile, and per-example qualitative flags.
  3) Produce a "regression heatmap" highlighting prompts/segments where open models diverge >2% from baseline.

- Acceptance thresholds we typically recommend for parity discussions:
  * Metric parity: within 2% absolute on primary metric (F1) OR no more than a 1% drop if latency/cost improvements are material.
  * Latency: median within +10% of baseline, P95 ideally not > +25%.

Attached: redwood_recommendation.pdf with a sample benchmark layout and cost calc notes. We'll include hosted vs dedicated cost buckets in the full report.

Let us know the sample QA and expected retention rules (we'll use ephemeral data handling unless you request otherwise).

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

If you can include that rubric in the first-pass report, we'll review and schedule a follow-up sync for 6/18 to go over the parity findings.
